scope: Seven existing Science pilot topics only; not the full NCERT curriculum or Maths.
input_language: English for all cases, to test the selected teaching-language preference independently.

reactions-signs: A chemical reaction produces new substances. Clues can include a gas being released, a colour change, a temperature change, or a precipitate. A clue alone is not always proof: boiling water also produces bubbles but is a physical change.
When magnesium burns, it reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide. The bright light and new white solid are signs of a chemical reaction.
Why is melting ice a physical change? It remains water; no new substance forms.
reactions-balance: Atoms are conserved during a chemical reaction. Balance an equation by changing coefficients in front of formulas, never the subscripts inside a formula.
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Both sides contain four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms.
Why must we not change H₂O to H₂O₂ to balance water formation? Changing subscripts changes the substance: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide.
reactions-types: In a combination reaction, two or more reactants form one product. In a decomposition reaction, one reactant breaks into two or more products. Displacement reactions involve a more reactive element replacing another.
CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ is a combination reaction.
Which type is a reaction with one reactant and multiple products? A decomposition reaction.
light-reflection: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Both angles are measured from the normal, an imaginary line perpendicular to the surface. The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
A ray arriving at 30° to the normal leaves at 30° to the normal.
If a ray makes 20° with the mirror surface, what is its angle of incidence? 70°, because the normal is perpendicular to the surface.
light-images: A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image of the same size as the object. The image appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
An object 2 m in front of a plane mirror has its image 2 m behind the mirror.
Can a plane mirror's virtual image be projected onto a screen? No. The rays only appear to come from behind the mirror.
life-nutrition: Green plants use light energy to make carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water during photosynthesis. Chlorophyll absorbs light, and oxygen is released.
A leaf takes in carbon dioxide through stomata. Roots absorb the water needed for photosynthesis.
What is the role of chlorophyll? It absorbs the light energy used in photosynthesis.
life-respiration: Cells break down food to release usable energy. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen. Breathing moves air into and out of the body; cellular respiration is a chemical process inside cells.
During exercise, muscles need more energy, so breathing and heart rate usually increase.
Are breathing and cellular respiration the same process? No. Breathing exchanges air; respiration releases energy from food in cells.
